chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and others, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from some of our companions, who said:

I wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan Ṣāḥib al-ʿAskar (عليه السلام): May I be made your ransom, what is the meaning of the saying of al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام), ‘Our hadith cannot be borne by a brought-near angel, nor by a sent prophet, nor by a believer whose heart Allah has tested for faith’?

So the reply came: The meaning of the saying of al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام), that neither an angel nor a prophet nor a believer can bear it, is that the angel cannot bear it until he conveys it to another angel, and the prophet cannot bear it until he conveys it to another prophet, and the believer cannot bear it until he conveys it to another believer.
So this is the meaning of the saying of my grandfather (عليه السلام).

key_terms.امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ قَلْبَهُ لِلْإِيمَانِ: whose heart Allah has tested and prepared for faith
key_terms.حَدِيثُنَا: the teachings and narrations of the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام)
key_terms.لَا يَحْتَمِلُهُ: cannot bear or carry it alone
key_terms.مَلَكٌ مُقَرَّبٌ: an angel brought near to Allah in rank
key_terms.نَبِيٌّ مُرْسَلٌ: a prophet sent with divine mission
key_terms.يُخْرِجَهُ: to bring it forth, meaning to convey or transmit it

ai.seo_question: What does the saying ‘Our hadith cannot be borne by a brought-near angel, a sent prophet, or a tested believer’ mean?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the statement about the difficulty of bearing the hadith of the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام) refers to the need to transmit and share it, not an absolute inability to receive it. Even angels, prophets, and believers bear such knowledge by passing it on to others of their kind, showing the gravity and depth of these teachings.
